issue_context.title: Implement `ToString()` on `System.Collections.DictionaryEntry`
issue_context.body:
`DictionaryEntry` still doesn't have a good display in the debugger or when printing it to a log.

Could we implement `ToString()` that returns `$"{Key} = {Value}"`, like `KeyValurPair<TKey,TValue>` has?
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ae46d07eb778fd9e1d4cdfe799a9e1ee7ed1d570/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Collections/Generic/KeyValuePair.cs#L46

Issue Details

Author: KirillOsenkov
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Collections`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -
So, should this be a change to how `ToString()` is implemented or would it make more sense to add a `DebuggerDisplayAttribute`?

I'd prefer `ToString()` because there are several advantages:

 * `ToString()` is useful in various other contexts, such as various text logs, format strings, interpolated strings, printf debugging, etc.
 * `KeyValuePair<TKey, TValue>` uses `ToString()`
 * compiler verifies correctness (vs. whatever you write in `DebuggerDisplay` is stringly typed)
 * you can place a breakpoint in `ToString()`
 * it's faster for the debugger (single eval call vs. interpreting the debugger display string)
It's so frustrating when you see a useless type name in the logs for example, where it could have been meaningful and helpful to have the actual values.

That's a good point, but unfortunately nobody writes it that way. Look at all existing DebuggerDisplay usages:
https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/DebuggerDisplayAttribute.cs,761078d4519dc54e,references

I just had to fix this recently because someone refactored code and forgot to update DebuggerDisplay:
https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/pull/6650/files

> That's a good point, but unfortunately nobody writes it that way.

Only because the feature is new and nobody's used it yet. But at the very least, any *new* applications of `DebuggerDisplay` could (and I believe *should*) make use of the new feature so that mistakes like the one you linked can be spotted at compile-time.
@KirillOsenkov would you expect to add any string escaping into `ToString`? I'd expect to make it consistent with perhaps Tuple or other similar classes
sure, anything is fine, ValueTuple, KVP, as long as it’s something.
curious how ToString looks for anonymous types and old Tuples

> curious how ToString looks for anonymous types and old Tuples

FWIW both prettyprint their contents.
Does it truncate if key or value is huge? And do we want it to?
It does not do any truncation. Scanning through all places where we override `ToString`, I see lots of instances where we emit or build unbounded strings; I haven't found any where we truncate.

review_comments: Key can be null as well (even though the nullable annotation suggests it shouldn't be).  It'd be good to add tests for that.  And for empty strings for both key and value.
